highlights.title: Chinese military researchers and tech giants caught using Claude — US frontier model, coded 16 air-defense suppression tools targeting Taiwan, drafted anti-torpedo specs, and fed 151 million training queries to Alibaba
highlights.description: Anthropic accuses China-linked actors of using its Claude models of weapon development, intelligence activities, distilling AI models.

highlights.title: Waymo robotaxi calls cops on riders handling loaded AR-style ghost gun — Waymo alerted San Francisco police, then juvenile riders were stopped and arrested
highlights.description: Following a tip-off from robotaxi firm Waymo, San Francisco police conducted a 'high-risk vehicle stop' and arrested two juveniles for illegal possession of a firearm.

highlights.title: Anthropic’s AI Warning May Weigh on Chips, But Trade Seen Intact
highlights.description: AI executives’ calls to slow development of the technology are likely to weigh on chipmaker and supply-chain stocks in the near term, but will probably have limited long-term impact as spending on computing infrastructure remains strong, market watchers say.

highlights.description: There is increasing evidence that Mexican drug cartels are diversifying into cryptocurrency mining and are using crypto platforms to launder their ill-gotten gains.

highlights.title: Apple’s new phones are here
highlights.description:
Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 143, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you're new here, welcome, new tech season is here, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.) 
This week, I've been devouring every iPhone Duo video I can find, clicking on the wonderful websites nominated for this year's Tiny Awards, catching up on the excellent Onimusha: Way of the Sword, reading Wildwood ahead of the upcoming movie, watching the new Taskmaster series, coming to grips with Link's new look in the Ocarina of Time remake, and fixing the flat tire on my toddler's stroller. I'm very proud of that …
Read the full story at The Verge.

highlights.description: Apple’s Safari browser gets a few helpful automation and personalization features in iOS 27.

highlights.title: Xi Pitches AI Vision at BRICS Summit as China Duels With US
highlights.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping has sought to turn the annual BRICS summit into another platform for championing Beijing’s vision for artificial intelligence, as it vies for global influence over the technology with the US.

highlights.title: China’s Data Regulator Plans Standards Push for Embodied AI
highlights.description: China’s data regulator said it plans to develop standards for embodied artificial intelligence and guide local authorities in related work, as demand for high-quality, diverse and large-scale datasets continues to grow.

highlights.title: Build a high-end AMD gaming PC for less — Ryzen 7 9800X3D bundle includes an X870E motherboard, 32GB DDR5, AIO cooler and a game for $1,109.99
highlights.description: The bundle pairs one of the best gaming CPUs available with a premium X870E motherboard and 32GB of DDR5-6000 memory, while also throwing in a 240mm AIO cooler and a free copy of Onimusha: Way of the Sword.

highlights.title: Xi says China will take lead to foster AI, tech cooperation among BRICS countries
highlights.description: China will take the lead to help foster artificial-intelligence collaboration and development among developing-economy countries, President Xi Jinping said.

ev_autonomous.title: AI Industry Faces Pressure to Slow the Race
ev_autonomous.description: The AI industry is confronting a growing tension between racing to build more powerful systems and concerns that those systems could become harder to understand and control. Joining David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend are Bloomberg Opinion Technology Columnist Parmy Olson and Bloomberg News Executive Editor Technology & Strategic Industries Mike Shepard. Olson and Shepard examine the commercial and national security forces driving development, the push for greater industry coordination and government oversight, and why meaningful guardrails remain difficult to establish. (Source: Bloomberg)
